question.text: Under the AIF Regulations, winding up of a scheme is triggered when:

answer.text: The fund's tenure (or extended tenure) ends and the scheme is wound up as per the fund documents

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Regulation 29 (workbook pp.68 and 220), winding up is triggered on the expiry of the tenure or extended tenure of the scheme in the absence of further unit-holder consent, when the trustees form an opinion that the scheme should be wound up in the investors' interests, when at least 75% of the investors (by value) pass a resolution to wind up, or when SEBI so directs in the investors' interests. Tenure expiry without the consent needed for further extension is the most common trigger. The Trap: Mere SEBI revocation of registration is not the listed trigger — the registration certificate is surrendered after the scheme is wound up. Investor demand for immediate exit is not a regulatory winding-up ground, and market volatility on its own does not trigger winding up. Note: Source references: NISM Series XIX-A workbook pp.68 and 220 (Regulation 29 winding-up triggers — tenure expiry, trustee opinion, 75% investor resolution, SEBI direction).
